title: Support Switch Control, Switch Access and Voice Control across tools and objects
body:
## Context

Switch and voice input are the two access paths that break first in a pen-first app, because both ride on top of correct semantics but fail for their own reasons: Voice Control needs the **spoken name to match the visible label** ('Tap Pen'), and Switch Control needs a **grouped scanning order** or reaching a tool costs dozens of steps. `docs/design/accessibility.md` §1 names the mechanisms per platform (iPadOS Switch Control + Voice Control, Android Switch Access + Voice Access, web keyboard/switch emulation) and §13 makes 'verified with Voice Control/Voice Access and Switch Control/Switch Access for tool-select + object-edit' an acceptance row. PRD-CO-332 states it as a MUST, and the Apple Accessibility Nutrition Label we intend to declare includes **Voice Control**, which is gated on completing **all** common tasks that way (`accessibility.md` §12, PRD-CO-339). This issue takes the chrome semantics from {{SN-A11Y-002}} and the focus system from {{SN-A11Y-008}} and makes them actually drivable by scanning and by voice.

## Scope

**In:** an audit-and-fix pass ensuring every actionable node exposes an action (`onTap`/`onLongPress`/custom action) **and** an accessible name identical to its visible label; **alternate voice names** for ambiguous controls (the pen tool answers to 'pen', 'pencil' and 'draw') via `accessibilityUserInputLabels` on iOS and the equivalent node text on Android through a small platform channel; **scan grouping** (`Semantics(container: true, explicitChildNodes: true)` + `MergeSemantics`) so Switch scanning steps toolbar -> palette -> page rail -> canvas objects instead of every leaf; ensuring canvas-object custom actions from {{SN-A11Y-004}} appear in the Switch Control action menu and TalkBack's actions menu; ensuring no affordance is reachable only by hover, dwell, drag or multi-finger gesture; verifying Voice Control 'Show Names'/'Show Numbers' overlays are not clipped or overlapped by the floating palette dock, page rail or audio bar; a written scripted protocol for both input modes.

**Out:** the semantics themselves ({{SN-A11Y-002}}); keyboard traversal and shortcuts ({{SN-A11Y-008}}); the non-drag alternatives ({{SN-A11Y-009}}); the canvas tree and its action set ({{SN-A11Y-003}}/{{SN-A11Y-004}}); the manual end-to-end audit run ({{SN-A11Y-017}}).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the Editor, Library, Search, Share and Settings screens, saying 'Tap <visible label>' activates every control; no control has an accessible name that differs from its visible label.
- [ ] Each of the 7 editor tools responds to at least two alternate voice names (for example 'pen'/'pencil', 'highlighter'/'marker'), registered per locale.
- [ ] With Switch Control/Switch Access group scanning, any editor tool is reachable in <= 6 scan steps from the canvas, and each region (toolbar, palette, page rail, canvas objects, audio bar) is one scan group.
- [ ] Every canvas-object custom action (delete, duplicate, change colour, bring-to-front, convert-to-text) is listed in the Switch Control action menu and TalkBack actions menu for that object.
- [ ] No function is reachable only via hover, dwell, drag or a multi-finger gesture; a scripted 'create note -> pick pen -> select object -> convert to text -> export' run completes with switches only, and again with voice only.
- [ ] Voice Control 'Show Numbers' labels render fully visible over the floating dock and page rail in all 17 looks + dark, including the translucent Glass/Y2K/wallpaper surfaces.

## Technical notes

Flutter exposes actions through `Semantics(button: true, onTap: ..., customSemanticsActions: ...)`; grouping through `Semantics(container: true, explicitChildNodes: true)`. Alternate input labels have no Flutter API today: add a narrow method channel in `plugins/sane_stylus`-style form or an app-level channel that sets `accessibilityUserInputLabels` on the `FlutterView`'s semantics elements (iOS) and augments `AccessibilityNodeInfo` (Android) - **verify both against the current SDK before implementing** and degrade to the primary label where unavailable. `MediaQuery.of(context).accessibleNavigation` indicates an AT is driving the UI: use it to disable dwell-only affordances and to prefer explicit buttons. Code lands in `app/lib/a11y/switch_voice.dart` plus per-screen fixes; keep `packages/sane_ui` a pure leaf (no platform channels there) per CLAUDE.md §3. Implements PRD-CO-332/PRD-CO-321 and `accessibility.md` §1/§13; ADR-0003 for state/app structure. Scheduled in M3: the object custom actions/descriptions it audits come from {{SN-A11Y-004}} (on-device OCR object descriptions, M3); its other dependencies are M1.

## Security & privacy

Assistive services are a platform trust boundary: anything exposed as a semantic label is readable by any enabled accessibility service. Therefore masked fields (phone OTP, recovery code, passphrase) MUST expose a role and name but **never their value** (MASVS-PLATFORM-3, CWE-200), and canvas object labels - which are user note content - MUST never be logged (MASVS-PRIVACY-3, CWE-532, CLAUDE.md §7.3). Correct platform a11y projection is itself the control (MASVS-PLATFORM-1). This issue adds no network egress; alternate-name tables are static localised strings shipped in the bundle.

## UX notes

Covers the Editor (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` Editor §7: toolbar, tool palette, page rail, audio bar, selection bar), Library §6, Search §11, Share §10 and Settings §12 per the per-screen map in `accessibility.md` §10. Labels use the product voice (`design-system.md` §1) - 'Pen', 'Highlighter', 'Convert to text' - so the spoken name and the tooltip agree. Verify the Show Numbers overlay against low-contrast looks (Cyberpunk/Glass light) where the OS overlay sits on a translucent surface; increase surface opacity behind chrome if the overlay is unreadable ({{SN-A11Y-007}}).

## Test plan

Widget: `app/test/a11y/switch_voice_labels_test.dart` walks the semantics tree of each top-level screen and asserts (a) every node with an action has a non-empty label, (b) labels are unique within a screen so voice targeting is unambiguous, (c) scan groups exist with the expected container structure. `app/test/a11y/masked_field_semantics_test.dart` is the negative test: an OTP/recovery-code field must not expose its value. Manual: the scripted protocol in `tools/device_lab/a11y-protocol.md` run on iPad (Switch Control + Voice Control) and Android (Switch Access + Voice Access).

## Dependencies

{{SN-A11Y-002}} (chrome semantics), {{SN-A11Y-008}} (focus order), {{SN-A11Y-004}} (object custom actions).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Ship the colour-blind-safe ink palette, colour names and simulation preview
body:
## Context

The shared ink palette (`INK` / `DARK_INK` / `HL` in `docs/design/design-system.md` §2) is a locked product constant and is **not** Okabe-Ito colour-blind-optimised - it contains a red (`#d33b3b`) / green (`#2e8b57`) pair that deuteranopes and protanopes cannot separate. `docs/design/accessibility.md` §5 records the decision and mandates three mitigations: (a) **every swatch carries a colour name**, (b) an **optional Okabe-Ito colour-blind-safe ink palette** the user can switch to, (c) a **colour-blind preview/simulation** mode. WCAG 1.4.1 additionally forbids encoding meaning in colour alone anywhere in the app, which is a cross-cutting audit, not a picker feature. PRD-CO-311 and PRD-CO-335 state all of this as MUST, and risk R5 in `prd-04` §11.3 records the retained default. The brushes area owns the picker surfaces ({{SN-BRS-020}} quick palette, {{SN-BRS-022}} per-notebook palettes and the colour-blind toggle UI); this issue owns the **shared data and rules they consume** plus the app-wide colour-alone audit.

## Scope

**In:** a `SaneColourNames` table in `packages/sane_ui` mapping every `INK`/`DARK_INK`/`HL`/`TINT` value and every subject colour to a **localised** name (near-black, blue, red, green, purple, orange; highlighter yellow/pink/green/blue) used by both the visible chip caption and the semantics label; the verified **Okabe-Ito** constants (`#000000, #E69F00, #56B4E9, #009E73, #F0E442, #0072B2, #D55E00, #CC79A7` - **verify the exact hex against the jfly source** before merging) plus dark-mode counterparts that keep >= 3:1 against `pp`; a colour-vision **simulation filter** (deuteranopia, protanopia, tritanopia) applied as a preview-only `ColorFilter.matrix` over the page; the app-wide **'never by colour alone'** audit and fixes (active tool = accent **plus** filled/weight; subject colour **plus** name; share role **plus** text; errors as toast text, never red-only); wiring the OS 'Differentiate Without Color' signal so those non-colour cues are forced on.

**Out:** the picker UI, per-notebook palettes and the `.sanepalette` file ({{SN-BRS-022}}); the quick palette row ({{SN-BRS-020}}); the chrome token palette and its adjusted contrast layer ({{SN-DS-002}}/{{SN-DS-006}}); high-contrast and reduce-transparency adaptation ({{SN-A11Y-007}}).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every swatch in every picker announces 'name, selected/not selected' (for example 'Blue, selected') and shows the name in its tooltip/caption; names come from the ARB pipeline and are translated.
- [ ] Switching on the colour-blind-safe palette replaces the six pen slots with the Okabe-Ito set for **future** picks only; strokes already drawn keep their stored colour (a palette changes what you pick, never what you drew).
- [ ] Each Okabe-Ito entry in both light and dark keeps >= 3:1 contrast against the default paper `pp` for all 17 looks, verified by a unit test.
- [ ] Simulation preview renders the current page under each of the three deficiency types, is clearly labelled as a preview, never mutates stored colours, and exits cleanly.
- [ ] An automated audit test finds zero interactive controls whose only difference between states is hue, and zero status/roles conveyed by colour alone.
- [ ] With the OS 'Differentiate Without Color' setting on, every selected/active state additionally shows a shape, fill or weight cue.

## Technical notes

Data lives in `packages/sane_ui/lib/src/colour_names.dart` and `packages/sane_ui/lib/src/palettes/okabe_ito.dart` as pure const data - `sane_ui` is a leaf package (CLAUDE.md §3) so no model or feature imports. Simulation uses `ColorFiltered` with the standard Brettel/Vienot matrices (document the matrix source in a comment). 'Differentiate Without Color' is read via `UIAccessibility.shouldDifferentiateWithoutColor` on iOS through a platform channel and treated as unavailable (default off) elsewhere - **verify against the current SDK**. Names are ARB keys resolved through {{SN-I18N-007}}'s pipeline. Per `design-system.md` (Shared drawing constants), the ink constants are cross-platform drawing data: the alternative palette selects which list the picker offers and is stored as a profile preference; it never rewrites `docs/design/tokens.json`. Implements PRD-CO-311/PRD-CO-335 and `accessibility.md` §5.

## Security & privacy

Beyond baseline this is low risk: the palette choice is a non-sensitive profile preference stored locally, no note content is involved, nothing is logged (CWE-532, MASVS-PRIVACY-3) and there is no network egress. The only platform interaction is reading an OS accessibility flag, which must fail closed to 'off' if the channel is unavailable (MASVS-PLATFORM-1). Colour names are static localised strings, not user data.

## UX notes

Surfaces: the colour row in the tool palette (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` Editor §7.3), the full picker ({{SN-BRS-021}} where it exists) and Settings -> Appearance (§12). Copy follows the product voice: 'Colour-blind-safe pens - swaps the six pens for a palette that stays distinct for every kind of colour vision'. Avoid new red/green adjacencies anywhere in chrome (use magenta + green, `accessibility.md` §5). Works in all 17 looks + dark; the simulation preview must itself remain legible (it filters the page, never the chrome).

## Test plan

Unit: `packages/sane_ui/test/colour_names_test.dart` (every ink/highlighter/tint constant has a name key; keys exist in the ARB) and `packages/sane_ui/test/okabe_ito_contrast_test.dart` (every entry >= 3:1 on `pp` per look x mode). Widget: `app/test/a11y/colour_not_alone_test.dart` walks each screen's semantics + render tree and fails on state pairs differing only in hue. Golden: `app/test/golden/colour_blind_simulation_test.dart` for the three simulations on a sample page. Manual: check a red/green annotated page under the simulation.

## Dependencies

{{SN-DS-002}} (tokens/ThemeExtension), {{SN-BRS-020}} (quick palette that consumes the names); coordinates with {{SN-BRS-022}} which builds the picker UI on top of this data.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Compose left-handed mode with RTL without breaking focus or reading order
body:
## Context

Left-handed mode and RTL are two different mirrors that are routinely conflated, and conflating them breaks both. `docs/design/gestures-and-shortcuts.md` §8 is explicit: left-handed mode (`prefs.leftHanded`, off by default) moves the **page rail to the left**, relocates the **palm-rejection zone** and the default palette dock side so the writing hand never covers the UI, and it does **not** mirror text or reading order; RTL mirrors app **chrome** and reading order via `Directionality`, and the **ink canvas is never mirrored** (a drawing is a drawing). `docs/design/accessibility.md` §9 and PRD-CO-337/PRD-CO-372 require the two settings to be **independent and compose correctly** - a right-handed Arabic user and a left-handed English user are different configurations - and require that left-handed mode must not break keyboard focus order or screen-reader reading order. {{SN-INK-016}} implements handedness for the ink surface and chrome and {{SN-I18N-007}} implements RTL mirroring; this issue owns the **composition matrix, the logical-order guarantee, and the regression gate** that keeps them from drifting apart.

## Scope

**In:** a documented four-cell matrix (LTR right-handed, LTR left-handed, RTL right-handed, RTL left-handed) stating the expected side for the page rail, the default palette dock edge, the palm-rejection/wrist-guard band, page-nav affordances and the audio bar; enforcing that handedness is applied as **visual placement only** (explicit child order / `row-reverse` equivalent) and never by wrapping a subtree in `Directionality`, which would also reverse text; explicit `OrdinalSortKey`/`SemanticsSortKey` on the editor regions so screen-reader and Tab order stay **logical** in all four cells; verifying the canvas is unmirrored under RTL; announcing the change when the toggle flips ('Page rail moved to the left'); and the golden + traversal regression tests that lock all four cells.

**Out:** the left-handed toggle and the ink-surface mirroring itself ({{SN-INK-016}}); RTL chrome mirroring and the locale pipeline ({{SN-I18N-007}}); the page rail widget ({{SN-ED-015}}/{{SN-PG-011}}); palette dock drag-to-dock ({{SN-ED-005}}); the Settings row that hosts the toggle ({{SN-SET-007}}).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four cells render per the documented matrix and are covered by goldens in at least three looks plus dark mode.
- [ ] Tab traversal order and screen-reader reading order are **identical** in all four cells (logical order), proven by a test comparing the traversal sequence of node identifiers.
- [ ] Under RTL the canvas content, stroke coordinates and page thumbnails are not mirrored; chrome is.
- [ ] The palm-rejection / wrist-guard band follows **handedness**, not directionality; the default dock edge follows handedness and a user-chosen dock edge always wins over the default.
- [ ] Toggling handedness announces the change, preserves editor state (open page, tool, selection, zoom), and needs no restart.
- [ ] With Arabic locale + left-handed mode on, keyboard shortcuts, focus rings and skip links from {{SN-A11Y-008}} still work; no widget uses `Directionality` to implement handedness (asserted by a test/lint).

## Technical notes

Read `prefs.leftHanded` from the profile preference provider ({{SN-SET-003}} once it lands; a local preference provider until then) and expose it as a Riverpod provider consumed by the editor shell in `app/lib/editor/`. Mirror layout by reversing children explicitly (`Row(children: leftHanded ? [...].reversed.toList() : [...])`) or by a dedicated `HandedRow` helper; never by `Directionality`. Pin reading order with `Semantics(sortKey: OrdinalSortKey(n))` on the shell regions so both mirrors are cosmetic to AT. RTL primitives (`EdgeInsetsDirectional`, `AlignmentDirectional`) stay reserved for directionality per {{SN-I18N-007}}. Implements PRD-CO-337/PRD-CO-372 and `gestures-and-shortcuts.md` §8; document the matrix in `docs/design/accessibility.md` §9 cross-reference.

## Security & privacy

None beyond baseline - layout and semantics ordering only. Baseline still applies: no note content, ink coordinates or preference values in logs (CWE-532, MASVS-PRIVACY-3, CLAUDE.md §7.3); no new network egress; correct semantics projection to the platform a11y API is the only platform control touched (MASVS-PLATFORM-1).

## UX notes

Mirrors the design's editor frame (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` Editor §7, page rail §7.6) with `row-reverse` for left-handed users; Settings copy is already fixed by {{SN-SET-007}}: 'Left-handed mode - Moves the page rail to the left so your hand never covers it'. Verify in all 17 looks + dark that the mirrored rail keeps its shadow/border treatment (per-look `--sh`, `--ln`) and that the dock edge guides still light up on the correct edges. Targets stay >= 44 pt / 48 dp after mirroring.

## Test plan

Widget: `app/test/a11y/handedness_rtl_matrix_test.dart` builds the editor in all four cells and asserts (a) traversal order equality, (b) semantics reading order equality, (c) rail/dock/palm-band sides per the matrix, (d) no `Directionality` widget introduced by the handedness path. Golden: `app/test/golden/editor_handedness_rtl_test.dart` (4 cells x 3 looks x light/dark). Manual: TalkBack in Arabic with left-handed mode on.

## Dependencies

{{SN-INK-016}} (left-handed mode for ink surface and chrome), {{SN-I18N-007}} (RTL chrome mirroring).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Add motor-assist presets: stabilisation, larger targets and single-touch mode
body:
## Context

`docs/design/accessibility.md` §9 asks for a genuinely inclusive motor-assist set: a **stroke-stabilisation slider** (off by default, with live preview, independent for pen and finger) including a **Motion Filtering** mode marketed as a **tremor aid**, a **single-touch gesture companion** (undo/redo/zoom/pan with one finger, the Procreate pattern) and **larger targets on request** while always honouring the 44 pt / 48 dp / 24 px platform floors (WCAG 2.5.8). The doc calls the tremor aid 'a genuinely inclusive, differentiating feature' - no competitor markets one. The engine pieces already exist as separate issues: the filters themselves ({{SN-INK-003}}), the 0-100 slider-to-parameter mapping and per-pen presets ({{SN-INK-017}}) and the single-touch companion recogniser ({{SN-ED-026}}). This issue assembles them into one discoverable, accessible offering with named presets and a live preview, so a user with a tremor can find and trust it in one place (PRD-CO-337, PRD-CO-320).

## Scope

**In:** a `MotorAssistPrefs` value object (stabilisationPen 0-100, stabilisationFinger 0-100, tremorFiltering on/off + amount, singleTouchMode on/off, largerTargets on/off, longPressDuration 300-1200 ms) with a Riverpod provider and persistence; four named presets (Off, Light, Strong, **Tremor aid**) mapped onto {{SN-INK-017}}'s parameters; a settings group with a **live preview** canvas that redraws a sample stroke as the slider moves; independent pen and finger values; `largerTargets` raising interactive targets (tool buttons 44 -> 56 pt, chips 34 -> 44, chrome buttons 42 -> 52) with spacing preserved and no clipping at 320 px / 200% text; `singleTouchMode` enabling the one-finger companion from {{SN-ED-026}} and surfacing its on-screen affordances; announcing every change to AT.

**Out:** the 1-euro / streamline / motion-filter implementation ({{SN-INK-003}}); the parameter mapping and per-pen defaults ({{SN-INK-017}}); the gesture recogniser and input precedence ({{SN-ED-026}}); the zoom writing window ({{SN-ED-019}}); the Settings tab shell and its stylus rows ({{SN-SET-007}}).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Stabilisation is **off by default**; changing the slider updates the live preview within one frame (<= 16.7 ms) and never blocks the UI isolate.
- [ ] Pen and finger stabilisation are independent: setting finger to 80 leaves pen output byte-identical.
- [ ] The Tremor aid preset reduces RMS deviation from the intended path by >= 40% on a synthetic jittered polyline fixture while keeping endpoint error <= 2 page units (unit test with a recorded tremor sample).
- [ ] With `largerTargets` on, every interactive target is >= 56 pt (iPadOS) / 56 dp (Android) and the editor, library and settings layouts still fit at 320 px width with 200% text, with no overlap or clipping.
- [ ] With `singleTouchMode` on, undo, redo, zoom in, zoom out, fit and pan are each achievable with one finger, each affordance is labelled for AT, and multi-finger gestures continue to work.
- [ ] Preferences persist per profile across restart; a profile switch swaps them; changing a setting posts an announcement ('Stabilisation: Tremor aid').
- [ ] `tools/perf_harness` shows no regression of the pen-down-to-pixel budget (<= 16 ms ProMotion iPad, <= 25 ms mid Android) with stabilisation at 100.

## Technical notes

Model and provider in `app/lib/a11y/motor_assist.dart`; persist through the per-profile preference repository ({{SN-SET-003}}) when it lands and through the local settings store until then (documented migration). The preview widget renders with the same `sane_ink` pipeline as the canvas so what you see is what you get; keep it out of the hot draw path (rebuild on value change, not per pointer sample - CLAUDE.md §8). `largerTargets` is applied by a `SaneTargets` inherited size policy read by `sane_ui` components rather than per-call-site padding, so one switch changes the whole app. Implements PRD-CO-337 (motor assist) and PRD-CO-320 (target size); grounding in `docs/design/accessibility.md` §9 and `docs/design/pen-and-brush-spec.md` §8.

## Security & privacy

Preferences hold no personal data and are stored locally with the rest of the profile preferences (MASVS-STORAGE-1: no sensitive data in plain preference storage). The live preview handles ink coordinates - these MUST never be logged (CWE-532, MASVS-PRIVACY-3, CLAUDE.md §7.3), and the preview never persists a stroke. No network egress. Reading OS pointer/accessibility capabilities uses the platform channel contract only (MASVS-PLATFORM-1).

## UX notes

Lives in Settings -> Handwriting & stylus ({{SN-SET-007}}) as a grouped 'Motor assist' section following the design's setting-row composite, with the product voice: 'Tremor aid - smooths out shake without flattening your handwriting'. The live preview matches the design sheet's card treatment across all 17 looks + dark. Preset chips are a radio group with names exposed to AT; sliders carry numeric values and honour the non-drag rule from {{SN-A11Y-009}} (numeric entry alternative). Empty/edge state: on a device with no stylus, the pen slider is disabled with an explanation rather than hidden.

## Test plan

Unit: `app/test/a11y/motor_assist_prefs_test.dart` (preset mapping, independence of pen/finger, persistence round-trip, migration path) and `app/test/a11y/tremor_reduction_test.dart` (RMS/endpoint assertions against `test/fixtures/tremor_polyline.json`). Widget: `app/test/a11y/larger_targets_test.dart` using `meetsGuideline(iOSTapTargetGuideline)`/`androidTapTargetGuideline` with the flag on and off. Golden: `app/test/golden/motor_assist_settings_test.dart`. Perf: a `tools/perf_harness` run at stabilisation 100 attached to the PR.

## Dependencies

{{SN-INK-003}} (filters), {{SN-INK-017}} (slider mapping and presets), {{SN-ED-026}} (single-touch companion recogniser).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Build reading mode with Read Aloud, dyslexia fonts and spacing controls
body:
## Context

`docs/design/accessibility.md` §7 specifies an Immersive-Reader-class **reading mode** for typed text and OCR transcripts (never raw ink): Read Aloud with word highlight, speed and voice; a **reading-font picker including OpenDyslexic and Lexend**; adjustable size and spacing meeting WCAG 1.4.12; theme and column controls; line focus; and translation. PRD-CO-336 states it as a MUST. This is the surface that makes a handwritten notebook usable for a dyslexic or low-vision student - a wedge no ink competitor offers, and it is only possible because Sane OCRs on-device ({{SN-HWR-001}}). {{SN-DS-010}} explicitly defers reading-mode fonts to this issue, and {{SN-STDY-005}} reuses this pipeline to read flashcards aloud. The privacy trap here is real: several platform text-to-speech voices synthesise **on a server**, which would quietly ship note content off-device and break locked decision 3 and PRD-CO-000.

## Scope

**In:** a full-screen reading surface opened from a page's overflow menu, from a transcript and from search results; single-column rendering of typed blocks plus the page's OCR transcript with the source page reference; a font picker (look body font, **OpenDyslexic**, **Lexend**) with bundled fonts + licences; size 12-48 px, line-height, paragraph, letter and word spacing controls whose ranges include and exceed the 1.4.12 minimums (1.5x / 2x / 0.12x / 0.16x); theme (look surface / sepia / high-contrast) and column-width controls; **line focus** masking 1/3/5 lines; **Read Aloud** with per-word highlight, 0.5x-2x speed, voice picker, play/pause, skip sentence and 'read from here'; persistence of all reading preferences per profile; an entry point that hands translation to Sage ({{SN-AI-001}}, PRD-CO-156) rather than implementing it here.

**Out:** the recognition engine and transcript production ({{SN-HWR-001}}); typed-text editing and its own a11y ({{SN-TXT-001}}); translation implementation ({{SN-AI-001}}); audio captions ({{SN-A11Y-015}}); syllable splitting, parts-of-speech and picture dictionary (recorded in Technical notes as a deliberate deferral - the docs list them as Immersive-Reader parity, not a MUST).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reading mode opens for any page that has typed text or an OCR transcript in < 500 ms on the mid-range Android reference device, and shows an honest empty state ('Nothing to read yet - convert handwriting to text first', linking convert-to-text) when neither exists.
- [ ] The font picker offers OpenDyslexic and Lexend; switching re-renders without layout break at any supported size, and spacing controls reach 1.5x line / 2x paragraph / 0.12x letter / 0.16x word with **no clipping or overlap** at 320 px width.
- [ ] Read Aloud highlights the spoken word within +/- 150 ms of the audio at 1x, 1.5x and 2x, resumes at the paused word, and stops when the surface closes or the app is backgrounded.
- [ ] **Read Aloud uses an on-device voice only**: voices that require network synthesis are filtered out of the picker; when no offline voice is installed the feature shows a clear state with a link to the OS voice settings and **never** sends text to a network TTS. Airplane-mode read-aloud works on a device with an installed offline voice.
- [ ] Raw ink is never rendered in reading mode and the source page is never modified; a correction made to the transcript here writes back through the recognition model's user-editable transcript, is undoable, and leaves the strokes untouched.
- [ ] The surface itself is accessible: every control labelled, keyboard-operable, focus visible, 44 pt / 48 dp targets, correct in all 17 looks + dark, and reduce-motion honoured ({{SN-A11Y-006}}).

## Technical notes

Code in `app/lib/a11y/reading_mode/`; text comes from `sane_core` typed blocks and the `sane_ml` transcript for the page ({{SN-HWR-001}}). TTS through a thin adapter (`app/lib/a11y/reading_mode/tts_adapter.dart`) over the platform engine with an **offline-voice filter**: iOS `AVSpeechSynthesisVoice.speechVoices()` preferring downloaded enhanced/premium voices; Android `TextToSpeech` rejecting any `Voice` with `isNetworkConnectionRequired == true` or the `networkSynthesis` feature; web `SpeechSynthesisVoice.localService == true`. **Verify each API against the current SDK before implementing** (PRD-04 convention). Fonts: bundle OpenDyslexic and Lexend beside the look families from {{SN-DS-009}}, with a `LICENSES.md` entry, version and provenance recorded for the SBOM. Long transcripts render with a lazy list; formatting recomputation stays off the UI isolate for large pages (CLAUDE.md §8). Implements PRD-CO-336 and `accessibility.md` §7.

## Security & privacy

Reading aloud is a **content egress path**: a network TTS voice would transmit note text to a third party, violating locked decision 3 / PRD-CO-000. Control: the voice filter above, enforced by a negative test, plus an assertion that the adapter has no HTTP client. Transcripts and typed text are user content - never log them (CWE-532, MASVS-PRIVACY-3) and keep processing on-device (MASVS-PRIVACY-2, MASVS-NETWORK-1). A locked notebook must not be readable through this surface (PRD-LOCK-006, MASVS-PLATFORM-3, CWE-200): reading mode refuses to open for a locked notebook until it is unlocked. Bundled fonts are third-party artefacts: pin versions, record licences and include them in the SBOM (MASVS-CODE-3).

## UX notes

Follows `accessibility.md` §7 and the design system's type scale (`design-system.md` §3) - reading mode is the **only** place OpenDyslexic/Lexend appear; look fonts stay for chrome. Entry points: page `...` menu, transcript panel, search result. Controls sit in a top bar (font, size, spacing, theme, line focus, Read Aloud) that collapses on narrow widths; all 17 looks + dark supported, with the high-contrast theme option reusing {{SN-A11Y-007}}'s variant. Loading state while a transcript is still being produced; error state if recognition failed, with a retry.

## Test plan

Widget: `app/test/a11y/reading_mode_test.dart` (controls, spacing ranges, no clipping at 320 px + 200%, persistence, locked-notebook refusal). Negative: `app/test/a11y/read_aloud_voice_filter_test.dart` injects a fake TTS exposing a network-only voice and asserts it is excluded and never spoken. Golden: `app/test/golden/reading_mode_test.dart` across three looks + dark and both fonts. Integration: `app/integration_test/reading_mode_test.dart` (open from a page, read aloud two sentences, correct a word, close). Manual: VoiceOver interaction with Read Aloud running.

## Dependencies

{{SN-HWR-001}} (OCR transcripts), {{SN-TXT-001}} (typed text model), {{SN-DS-009}} (font bundling pattern), {{SN-DS-010}} (type scale / SaneText).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Provide time-synced captions and assistive-reachable media controls for audio
body:
## Context

Lecture audio pinned to ink is a headline Sane feature, which makes it an accessibility obligation: `docs/design/accessibility.md` §11 requires that **every recording offers time-synced captions plus a searchable transcript**, and that media controls (play/pause/stop, seek, speed) are keyboard and assistive-technology reachable. PRD-CO-338 states it as a MUST, and 'Captions' is one of the eight Apple Accessibility Nutrition Label features we intend to declare truthfully (§12, PRD-CO-339) - a label that is only declarable if captions cover the common tasks. The transcription pipeline with aligned word timings already exists ({{SN-AUD-020}}) and the transcript panel with export and search exists ({{SN-AUD-021}}); what is missing is the **caption presentation synced to playback** and the **accessible transport**, which this issue delivers on top of the recorder bar ({{SN-AUD-010}}).

## Scope

**In:** caption segmentation as a pure function over word timings (<= 2 lines, <= 42 characters per line, >= 1 s dwell, sentence-aware splitting, gap handling); a caption view over the playback surface showing the current segment with the spoken word highlighted; a captions on/off + caption size preference persisted per profile; accessible transport - play/pause/stop labelled with state, the scrubber exposed as a semantic slider announcing `mm:ss of mm:ss` and moving in 5 s steps via arrow keys or AT increment/decrement, speed control announcing its value; the canvas audio-anchor node announcing 'audio at 04:12' with a **play** custom action feeding {{SN-A11Y-004}}'s action set; caption export to **WebVTT and SRT** alongside the existing transcript export.

**Out:** recording and playback services ({{SN-AUD-002}}); transcription and word alignment ({{SN-AUD-020}}); the transcript panel, its search and its plain-text export ({{SN-AUD-021}}); the recorder bar visual design ({{SN-AUD-010}}); reading mode ({{SN-A11Y-014}}); translation of captions ({{SN-AI-001}}).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every recording that has a transcript offers captions; the on/off choice and caption size persist per profile and survive restart.
- [ ] Captions track playback within +/- 150 ms at 1x, 1.5x and 2x and re-sync within 200 ms after a scrub or a skip.
- [ ] Segments never exceed 2 lines or 42 characters per line; a word longer than the line budget wraps rather than being clipped; a > 3 s silence produces no caption rather than a stale one.
- [ ] Caption text renders at >= 4.5:1 against its scrim in every look x light/dark, scales with Dynamic Type to 200% without covering the scrubber, and is never rendered directly over the waveform.
- [ ] Every transport control exposes name/role/state/value; the scrubber announces `mm:ss of mm:ss`, responds to AT increment/decrement and to arrow keys with a 5 s step, and play/pause state changes are announced.
- [ ] A recording whose transcript is not ready shows an honest state ('Transcript not ready - captions appear when it finishes'); everything works offline with no network call.
- [ ] Exported `.vtt` and `.srt` files open in a standard player with correct timings, and export happens only to a user-chosen location.

## Technical notes

Segmentation is pure Dart in `packages/sane_audio/lib/src/captions.dart` (unit-testable, no Flutter import beyond what the package already allows); the caption view and transport semantics live in `app/lib/audio/captions/`. Consume the aligned word timings produced by {{SN-AUD-020}} and the playback position stream from the audio service; do not re-run recognition. Slider semantics use `Semantics(slider: true, value:, increasedValue:, decreasedValue:, onIncrease:, onDecrease:)` so VoiceOver/TalkBack can scrub. Caption rendering uses a scrim surface from `sane_ui` rather than a per-look colour guess, so contrast holds across looks ({{SN-DS-006}} adjusted tokens where the accent is weak). Implements PRD-CO-338, PRD-LB-212/220 (audio anchors) and `accessibility.md` §3.2/§11; ADR-0015 (audio pipeline) governs the underlying pipeline.

## Security & privacy

Transcripts and captions are **note content**: generated on-device ({{SN-AUD-020}}, MASVS-PRIVACY-2), never sent anywhere (MASVS-NETWORK-1), and never written to logs (CWE-532, MASVS-PRIVACY-3, CLAUDE.md §7.3). Caption export must write only to the user-selected path with canonicalised, confined paths (CWE-22, secure-coding checklist §1) and must not leak into shared caches. A locked notebook must not surface captions in previews, the lock screen or a widget (PRD-LOCK-006, MASVS-PLATFORM-3). Cached caption files derived from a recording are stored beside the encrypted blob and follow the same at-rest rules (MASVS-STORAGE-2); they are removed when the recording is deleted.

## UX notes

Builds on the audio bar from the design (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` Editor §7.5 - play/pause, current time, waveform + scrubber, total duration, speed 1x/1.5x/2x, 'Ink replays in sync'). Captions appear above the bar in a compact two-line block with a scrim; a CC toggle sits next to the speed control and is labelled with state. Copy follows the product voice - 'Captions - read along with what was said'. Works in all 17 looks + dark, including translucent Glass/Y2K surfaces where the scrim must be strengthened. Reduce-motion suppresses any caption slide-in ({{SN-A11Y-006}}).

## Test plan

Unit: `packages/sane_audio/test/captions_test.dart` covering segmentation edge cases (single word longer than the line budget, long silences, overlapping timings, empty transcript) and WebVTT/SRT serialisation. Widget: `app/test/a11y/audio_transport_semantics_test.dart` asserts labels, slider value/increment behaviour and announcements. Golden: `app/test/golden/audio_captions_test.dart` in three looks + dark at 100% and 200% text. Integration: `app/integration_test/audio_captions_test.dart` (record 20 s, play, verify caption sync after a scrub, export `.vtt`).

## Dependencies

{{SN-AUD-010}} (recorder/playback bar), {{SN-AUD-020}} (aligned word timings), {{SN-AUD-021}} (transcript panel and export).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Automate accessibility tests: semantics, targets, contrast and axe on web
body:
## Context

Accessibility is a **build gate, not a phase** (`docs/design/accessibility.md` preamble): a surface is not done until it passes the criteria there, which only holds if CI can prove it on every pull request. {{SN-DS-029}} already covers `sane_ui` components in isolation; what is missing is the **screen-level** suite - real screens, real window sizes, real looks - plus the web surface, which `accessibility.md` §3.1 flags as historically the weakest ('Test Flutter web semantics explicitly'). PRD-CO-312/315/316/320/321 all need machine-checkable evidence, and the M7 audit ({{SN-A11Y-017}}) must start from a codebase that is already clean, not discover hundreds of violations. This issue builds the harness, the baselines and the CI job.

## Scope

**In:** an app-level suite under `app/test/a11y/` with a reusable `expectScreenAccessible(tester, {look, brightness, size})` helper running Flutter's built-in guideline matchers (`textContrastGuideline`, `androidTapTargetGuideline`, `iOSTapTargetGuideline`, `labeledTapTargetGuideline`) for each top-level screen across the compact/medium/expanded window classes and a representative look set (including the low-contrast offenders Pop, Glass, Cyberpunk, Neo-Brutalism light); a **semantics snapshot** per screen written as a text golden so label regressions are visible in review; an **axe-core** run (Playwright + `@axe-core/playwright`) against the built Flutter web app covering landmarks, document title, `lang`, focus order and colour contrast, with a versioned baseline allow-list where every entry carries an owner and an expiry date; a CI job wired into the existing DevSecOps workflow that runs the Dart suite on every PR and the web run on web-affecting PRs, publishing a report artifact; a coverage check failing when a new top-level screen has no a11y test.

**Out:** per-component tests ({{SN-DS-029}}); the token contrast codegen gate ({{SN-DS-007}}); the manual multi-screen-reader audit ({{SN-A11Y-017}}); perf gates ({{SN-PERF-003}}); the PR-template/lint gate ({{SN-A11Y-019}}).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Dart a11y suite runs in CI on every PR in < 6 minutes and fails with the offending widget path and matcher name when a label is missing, a target is under 44 pt / 48 dp / 24 px, or text contrast drops below 4.5:1.
- [ ] At least 10 screens are covered (Login, Profiles, Onboarding, Library, Editor, Templates, Import, Share, Search, Settings) at three window classes and four looks x light/dark.
- [ ] Semantics snapshots exist per screen; changing a label fails the diff and the update is an explicit, reviewable commit.
- [ ] The axe run reports **0 serious/critical** violations against the built web app; allow-listed exceptions fail the build once their expiry date passes.
- [ ] Flutter web semantics is explicitly enabled in the web harness and a smoke test asserts the semantics tree is present (not just an empty placeholder).
- [ ] A new top-level screen without an a11y test fails the coverage check with a message naming the missing test file.
- [ ] The job publishes a machine-readable report (JSON) plus a human summary as a CI artifact, containing **no** note content.

## Technical notes

Use `flutter_test`'s `meetsGuideline` matchers with a `SemanticsHandle`; drive screens through the `pumpApp(...)` harness from {{SN-QA-004}} and reuse the look matrix from {{SN-QA-005}}. The web harness lives in `tools/a11y_web/` (Node, `package-lock.json` committed, `npm ci`, exact pinned versions of Playwright and `@axe-core/playwright`, no floating ranges) and serves the release web build locally. Add the job to `.github/workflows/devsecops.yml` (or a sibling `a11y.yml` invoked from it) with least-privilege `permissions:` and SHA-pinned actions per {{SN-CI-001}}'s conventions. Test fixtures use synthetic notes only. Implements PRD-CO-312/315/316/320/321 and `accessibility.md` §13; complements {{SN-DS-007}}'s numeric token gate rather than duplicating it.

## Security & privacy

CI supply chain is the live risk: pin the Node toolchain and every a11y dependency by exact version with a committed lockfile and verify integrity, since an unpinned test dependency runs with repository-level permissions (OWASP-A06, MASVS-CODE-3, CWE-1104). The workflow must not send source or artifacts to a third-party service; axe runs locally in the runner. Report artifacts must contain no note content or personal data - the suite uses synthetic fixtures and redacts text values in snapshots where they would echo content (MASVS-PRIVACY-3, CWE-532). Least-privilege token scopes and SHA-pinned actions per the DevSecOps pipeline doc.

## UX notes

No user-facing UI. The suite encodes the design system's own rules, so it must read the adjusted tokens from {{SN-DS-006}} (never raw palette values) when asserting contrast, and it must assert the look-independent rules (labels, targets, focus) across the 17 looks + dark rather than sampling only Paper. Failure messages should name the screen, look, mode and window class so a designer can reproduce the state in the Widgetbook gallery ({{SN-DS-028}}).

## Test plan

This issue *is* tests, so the deliverables are: `app/test/a11y/a11y_harness.dart` (the helper), `app/test/a11y/screens_a11y_test.dart` (the matrix run), `app/test/a11y/semantics_snapshot_test.dart` (+ `app/test/a11y/snapshots/*.txt`), `tools/a11y_web/axe.spec.ts` and `tools/a11y_web/baseline.json`. Meta-tests: a deliberately broken fixture screen (missing label, 20 px target, 2:1 text) must fail each matcher, proving the harness detects rather than passes silently; the expiry logic is unit-tested with a past date.

## Dependencies

{{SN-A11Y-002}} (chrome semantics to assert), {{SN-QA-004}} (widget-test harness), {{SN-DS-029}} (component suite conventions), {{SN-CI-001}} (CI pipeline).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Run the pre-beta accessibility audit and declare the store accessibility labels
body:
## Context

M7 exists to prove the guarantees before real users arrive, and `docs/roadmap.md` M7 lists an **accessibility audit (WCAG 2.2 AA; VoiceOver/TalkBack; OCR alt-text)** as a delivered activity with 'WCAG 2.2 AA met on all chrome' as an exit criterion. `docs/design/accessibility.md` §13 is the audit instrument: a per-platform acceptance checklist covering contrast, scaling, colour, targets, gesture alternatives, keyboard, canvas semantics, assistive-technology verification, inclusive reading, motor assist, OCR/audio and i18n. §12 then defines the payoff: the eight **Apple Accessibility Nutrition Label** features (VoiceOver, Voice Control, Larger Text, Dark Interface, Differentiate Without Color, Sufficient Contrast, Reduced Motion, Captions), each declarable only if **all** common tasks can be completed with that feature, plus a clean Google Play pre-launch accessibility report (PRD-CO-339). This issue runs that audit, tracks its findings, and produces the evidence behind each declaration.

## Scope

**In:** turning `accessibility.md` §13 into a scored audit matrix with one row per criterion per platform; executing the scripted **common-task flows** (create a notebook, write ink, convert to text, search, share, export, play a recording with captions) end-to-end with **VoiceOver** (iPadOS), **TalkBack** (Android), **NVDA and JAWS** (web), plus **Voice Control/Voice Access** and **Switch Control/Switch Access** for tool selection and object editing; running **Xcode Accessibility Inspector**, **Android Accessibility Scanner** and the **Play Console pre-launch accessibility report**; the 200% text / 320 px reflow / text-spacing pass; the Reduce Motion, Increase Contrast, Differentiate Without Color, Bold Text and Reduce Transparency passes; a contrast sweep over all 17 looks x light/dark consuming {{SN-DS-007}}'s gate output; a findings log with severity where P0/P1 block beta, each finding filed as an issue in the owning area with a reproduction; and the evidence pack per nutrition-label feature.

**Out:** fixing the findings (each lands in the owning area's issue); the conformance statement and in-app page ({{SN-A11Y-018}}); the automated suite ({{SN-A11Y-016}}); store **privacy** labels ({{SN-PRV-015}}) and App Store Connect submission mechanics ({{SN-IPAD-023}}); the i18n/RTL audit (owned by {{SN-I18N-001}}).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every row of `accessibility.md` §13 has a pass/fail verdict **with evidence** (screen recording, Inspector/Scanner export or test output) for iPadOS, Android and Web.
- [ ] The common-task flow completes end-to-end with each of VoiceOver, TalkBack and NVDA (and JAWS for the web build), with the run recorded.
- [ ] Tool selection and object editing are completed once with Voice Control/Voice Access and once with Switch Control/Switch Access on both mobile platforms.
- [ ] Accessibility Inspector and Accessibility Scanner runs are clean, or every exception is recorded with a justification and a tracking issue; the Play pre-launch accessibility report shows no errors.
- [ ] All P0/P1 findings are fixed (with a regression test) or explicitly risk-accepted in writing by the maintainer before the beta gate; the audit is re-run after fixes and is green.
- [ ] Each of the eight Apple Accessibility Nutrition Label features has a completed common-task evidence pack **before** it is declared; a feature without complete evidence is **not** declared.
- [ ] The audit report is stored at `docs/design/accessibility-audit-<date>.md` and contains no note content, tester names or device identifiers.

## Technical notes

Run on the physical Tier 1/2 devices defined by {{SN-PERF-004}} (ProMotion iPad, mid-range Android tablet, low-end 4 GB Android, plus Chrome and Safari desktop for web). Use release-flavour builds so the audit reflects shipping behaviour (tree-shaken debug affordances, no auth bypass). Automate everything automatable first by running {{SN-A11Y-016}}'s suite and attaching its report, so the manual time is spent on the assistive-technology flows machines cannot judge. Record the protocol in `tools/device_lab/a11y-protocol.md` so the audit is repeatable each release. Maps to PRD-CO-310..339 and `docs/roadmap.md` M7 exit criteria; the SSDLC verification-stage rules in `docs/security/ssdlc-process.md` §2.4 govern findings handling.

## Security & privacy

Audit evidence is a privacy hazard in itself: screen recordings can capture note content and account identifiers, so the audit uses **synthetic fixture notebooks only**, and recordings are reviewed and redacted before they are attached (MASVS-PRIVACY-1 data minimisation, MASVS-PRIVACY-3, CWE-532). Verify during the audit that masked fields (OTP, recovery code, passphrase) expose no value to assistive technology and that locked notebooks stay unreadable through AT surfaces (MASVS-PLATFORM-3, PRD-LOCK-006). Correct platform a11y integration is the control being verified (MASVS-PLATFORM-1). Store declarations must be truthful - an over-claimed label is both a store-compliance and a legal risk (EAA/ADA).

## UX notes

The audit covers every screen in `design/Sane Notes.dc.html` per the per-screen map in `accessibility.md` §10 - Login, Profiles, Onboarding, Sidebar, Library, Editor, Templates, Import PDF, Share, Search, Settings, Upgrade and the global Toast - in all 17 looks x light/dark, with special attention to the light-mode looks flagged in §4.1 (Pop, Glass, Clay, Flat, Retro, Cyberpunk button labels; Neo-Brutalism and Cyberpunk accent icons; Neumorphism muted text) and to wallpaper mode's translucent surfaces.

## Test plan

Deliverables are the audit itself: the scored matrix (`docs/design/accessibility-audit-<date>.md`), the recorded AT runs, the Inspector/Scanner/pre-launch exports, the findings issues, and the nutrition-label evidence pack. Automated inputs: {{SN-A11Y-016}}'s report and {{SN-DS-007}}'s contrast gate output. Every fixed finding must ship with a regression test in its owning area (CLAUDE.md §10).

## Dependencies

{{SN-A11Y-016}} (automated suite and report), {{SN-A11Y-010}} (Switch/Voice support), {{SN-A11Y-014}} (reading mode), {{SN-A11Y-015}} (captions); device lab from {{SN-PERF-004}}. **needs-credentials:** App Store Connect access to declare nutrition labels and Play Console access to run the pre-launch report.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Publish the accessibility conformance statement and in-app accessibility page
body:
## Context

An accessibility audit that nobody can read is not a commitment. `docs/design/accessibility.md` sets the baseline as 'WCAG 2.2 AA on every platform, plus EN 301 549 / Section 508 / ADA / EU EAA where applicable', and PRD-CO-411 requires the docs site to host an **accessibility statement** alongside the format spec and privacy documentation. The European Accessibility Act expects a published, honest statement with known limitations and a feedback route; procurement and institutional buyers (schools, universities - our first persona is a student) routinely ask for a **VPAT/ACR**. This issue turns {{SN-A11Y-017}}'s evidence into three artefacts: the conformance report in the repo, an in-app Accessibility page, and the public statement on the docs site - all saying the same true things.

## Scope

**In:** `docs/design/accessibility-conformance.md`, a VPAT 2.5-style ACR mapping every WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA success criterion (plus the EN 301 549 and Section 508 rows that differ) to Supports / Partially Supports / Does Not Support / Not Applicable with a remark sourced from the audit evidence; an in-app **Accessibility** page reachable from About/Help ({{SN-SET-015}}) that lists supported features (screen reader support for chrome and handwriting, larger text, captions, reduce motion, colour-blind-safe pens, motor assist, full keyboard access), states the known limitations honestly (freehand path input is exempt as an essential analog gesture; recognition quality varies with handwriting; Flutter web semantics caveats) and offers a feedback route; the same statement rendered on the docs site (`website/`); a versioning rule (statement carries app version + date) and a re-verification step added to the release checklist.

**Out:** running the audit ({{SN-A11Y-017}}); declaring the store nutrition labels ({{SN-A11Y-017}}/{{SN-IPAD-023}}); the privacy policy and privacy labels ({{SN-PRV-017}}/{{SN-PRV-015}}); marketing copy about accessibility (website area - this issue supplies the facts it must not exceed).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The ACR covers every WCAG 2.2 A and AA success criterion with a verdict and a remark; no criterion is left blank.
- [ ] Every 'Supports' claim traces to a named piece of audit evidence from {{SN-A11Y-017}}; a criterion without evidence is recorded as 'Partially Supports' or 'Does Not Support' with the gap and its tracking issue.
- [ ] The in-app page is reachable in <= 3 taps from Settings, renders offline, and is itself accessible (semantics, 200% text, 44 pt targets, keyboard) - verified by the {{SN-A11Y-016}} suite like any other screen.
- [ ] The docs-site page is published, linked from the site footer, and a CI link check passes; the statement carries the app version, the audit date and a contact route for accessibility feedback.
- [ ] The release checklist gains a 'accessibility statement re-verified for this version' step, and the statement is regenerated whenever the audit is re-run.
- [ ] No claim in marketing copy exceeds the statement (checked once at publication).

## Technical notes

Write the ACR in Markdown in `docs/design/accessibility-conformance.md` following the VPAT 2.5 INT structure (WCAG 2.2 + EN 301 549 + Section 508 tables) so it can be exported for procurement. The in-app page is a static, localised screen in `app/lib/settings/accessibility_page.dart` reusing `SaneText` roles ({{SN-DS-010}}) and rendering from bundled localised content - no network fetch, so it works offline (locked decision: local-first). The website page renders the same source file through the docs pipeline so the two cannot drift. Dates and versions come from the build metadata used by the About screen ({{SN-SET-015}}). Implements PRD-CO-411 and `accessibility.md` §12/§13.

## Security & privacy

Documentation only, but publishing is an egress of information about our own systems and testers: the statement and ACR MUST NOT include device identifiers, tester names, internal hostnames, note content or screenshots containing real content (MASVS-PRIVACY-1 minimisation, MASVS-PRIVACY-3; CWE-532 for any log excerpt quoted). The in-app page ships as bundled assets with no network call, so it cannot become a tracking surface. Accuracy is a compliance control in its own right: an overstated conformance claim is a legal exposure under the EAA/ADA and a store-listing risk.

## UX notes

The in-app page follows the Settings About/Help pattern (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` Settings §12) - section headings, plain-language rows, no jargon - in the product voice: 'What works today, what does not yet, and how to tell us.' Renders in all 17 looks + dark, at 200% text, with no fixed-height rows that clip. The feedback route is a labelled link, not an email address rendered as an image. The docs-site page matches the site's typographic scale and passes its Lighthouse accessibility budget (PRD-CO-410).

## Test plan

Docs: a CI check that the ACR contains a row for every WCAG 2.2 A/AA criterion (a small script comparing against a committed criteria list) and that no verdict cell is empty. Widget: `app/test/a11y/accessibility_page_test.dart` (renders offline, semantics labels present, no clipping at 200% text and 320 px). Link check on the docs-site page in the website CI. Manual: read the statement against the audit report and confirm every claim is supported.

## Dependencies

{{SN-A11Y-017}} (audit evidence); consumes {{SN-SET-015}} (About/Help host screen) and {{SN-A11Y-016}} (the suite that tests the new page).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Enforce the accessibility checklist as a pull-request and CI gate
body:
## Context

`docs/design/accessibility.md` opens by declaring accessibility 'a **build gate**, not a phase - a surface is not done until it passes the criteria here', and CLAUDE.md §5 already requires the PR template's UX checklist (17 looks + dark mode, latency budget, a11y, empty/loading/error/offline). In practice a checklist only holds if something fails when it is ignored. {{SN-SEC-003}} proved the pattern for secure coding: a specific checklist in the PR template plus an automated rule that fails the build. This issue does the same for accessibility so that regressions are caught at authoring time - months before the M7 audit ({{SN-A11Y-017}}) - and so a new contributor or autonomous agent is told, in the diff, exactly which a11y obligation they missed.

## Scope

**In:** expanding the accessibility line in `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` into an explicit block (semantics name/role/state/value on new controls; target >= 44 pt / 48 dp / 24 px; colours via adjusted tokens, never hard-coded; reduce-motion honoured; keyboard path with visible focus; a non-gesture alternative for any new gesture or drag; layout survives 200% text at 320 px; alt-text for any new content type; no colour-only signal) with a required 'not applicable because ...' line; a Semgrep rule set `tools/semgrep/a11y.yml` that fails a PR adding, under `app/lib/**` or `packages/sane_ui/**`, an interactive `GestureDetector`/`InkWell`/`CustomPaint` surface without an enclosing `Semantics`/`ExcludeSemantics`, an `Image(`/`Icon(` without `semanticLabel`, or a hard-coded `Color(0x...)`/hex literal in UI code; wiring the rules into the existing DevSecOps workflow (warning-only for two weeks, then blocking) with a pinned Semgrep version; and a documented waiver comment `// A11Y-WAIVER: <reason> (<issue key>)` that suppresses a finding only when it carries a tracking issue key.

**Out:** the screen-level and web test suites ({{SN-A11Y-016}}); the component suite ({{SN-DS-029}}); the token contrast gate ({{SN-DS-007}}); the audit ({{SN-A11Y-017}}); writing the semantics themselves ({{SN-A11Y-002}}).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The PR template contains the accessibility block verbatim from `accessibility.md` §13's per-platform checklist, condensed to the nine authoring-time items, each a checkbox.
- [ ] `tools/semgrep/a11y.yml` flags a seeded violation fixture for each rule (unlabelled interactive surface, unlabelled image, hard-coded colour) and reports zero findings on a clean fixture.
- [ ] A waiver comment without an issue key does **not** suppress the finding; with a valid key it does, and the key is echoed in the CI output.
- [ ] The rules run in the DevSecOps workflow in < 60 s, with a pinned Semgrep version and no remote rule fetching (`--config tools/semgrep/a11y.yml --metrics=off`).
- [ ] After the two-week warning window the job is blocking, and the switch is a one-line, reviewed change recorded in the workflow file.
- [ ] The gate is documented in `docs/design/accessibility.md` cross-references and in CLAUDE.md §4's pre-flight checklist, so an agent reads it before starting an issue.

## Technical notes

Follow the structure of {{SN-SEC-003}}'s secure-coding gate: rules as data in `tools/semgrep/`, invoked from `.github/workflows/devsecops.yml` with least-privilege `permissions:` and SHA-pinned actions per {{SN-CI-001}}. Dart pattern rules in Semgrep are regex/AST-lite: keep them conservative (favour false negatives over noisy false positives) and document each rule's intent and known blind spots inline. The hard-coded-colour rule must exempt `packages/sane_ui/lib/src/tokens/**` (the generated token layer from {{SN-DS-002}}) and test fixtures. Semantics fixtures live in `tools/semgrep/fixtures/a11y/`. Complements the runtime assertions in {{SN-A11Y-016}}: static rules catch authoring mistakes, tests catch behavioural ones.

## Security & privacy

CI configuration changes are supply-chain surface: pin the Semgrep version and any action by commit SHA, disable metrics/telemetry upload, and never pass `--config auto` (which fetches remote rules at build time) - an unpinned or remote rule set executes in a job that can read the repository (OWASP-A06, MASVS-CODE-3, CWE-1104). The job must not upload source or diffs to a third-party service. CI logs must not echo file contents beyond the matched line (CWE-532). No application behaviour changes, so no runtime threat surface is added.

## UX notes

None beyond baseline for end users - this is repository tooling. Developer experience matters, though: failure messages name the file, line, the rule, the WCAG criterion it protects (for example '2.5.8 Target Size') and the fix, matching the product's plain-language voice so the gate teaches rather than scolds. The PR template block is short enough that reviewers actually read it.

## Test plan

`tools/semgrep/fixtures/a11y/violations.dart` and `clean.dart` plus a CI step asserting the expected finding counts (3 and 0) - the meta-test that proves the gate detects rather than passes silently. A waiver fixture verifies both the keyed and unkeyed cases. Manual: open a draft PR that adds an unlabelled icon button and confirm the annotation appears inline on the diff.
